title: GPU tenant profiling and fairness benchmark notebook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This notebook documents the GPU tenant profiling and fairness benchmarking toolkit we use to exercise heterogeneous tenant mixes against the allocation, warm-pool and preemption policies. The goal is to provide a repeatable, auditable benchmark that surfaces capacity fairness regressions, noisy-neighbor effects, and billing/cost-signal distortions before changes are rolled to production.

Why this exists
- Production incidents repeatedly show that aggregate SLOs can hide per-tenant poor performance.
- New allocator changes, topology packing, and spot-preemption heuristics introduce non-obvious distributional effects.
- We need an automated, CI-friendly harness that encodes realistic tenant behavior and fairness metrics.

Scope and audience
- Audience: infra engineers, SREs, platform product managers.
- Scope: simulation and small-scale shadow runs against staging GPU pools; NOT a full prod audit.
- What it does: generates tenant traffic profiles, runs them through the scheduler/allocator, collects latency, eviction, and cost metrics, then computes fairness/inequity scores.

Key concepts and definitions
- Tenant profile: a parametric workload (request rate, sequence length distribution, burstiness, prefix cache hit rate).
- Fairness window: 1h sampling window used to compute relative performance differences between tenants.
- Inequity score: Gini-like coefficient of token latency or tokens-per-dollar across tenants.
- SLO violation fraction: fraction of requests per tenant exceeding configured latency SLO.

Benchmark methodology
1. Select topology snapshot: region, pool type (on-demand / spot / hybrid), GPU flavor.
2. Define tenant mix: weights and profile parameters for 20–200 synthetic tenants.
3. Run simulation: feed synthetic traffic into the staging allocator via the test harness or via a shadow path that records placement decisions.
4. Collect metrics: per-tenant latency histogram, eviction counts, billing-sampled tokens, preemption events, and KV-cache hit rates.
5. Compute fairness metrics and produce a regression report.
6. Threshold check: if inequity_score > 0.18 or heavy-tail SLO_violation_fraction > 2%, fail the gate and open a regression issue.

Simulator configuration (example table)
| field | example | description |
| region | us-west-2 | region snapshot to use for topology allocation |
| pool_type | hybrid-spot | pool flavor under test (on-demand/spot/hybrid) |
| tenants | 80 | number of synthetic tenants |
| burstiness | 0.6 | 0..1 where 1 is extreme burstiness |
| seq_len_dist | 2,32,128 | percentiles (p10,p50,p90) to seed seq length sampler |
| cache_hit_rate | 0.22 | simulated prefix/KV cache hit probability |

Running the harness (CLI snippets)
- Run a full simulation locally against the staging allocator snapshot:

  export TOPOLOGY_SNAPSHOT=snap-2025-02-01
  python bench/harness.py --snapshot $TOPOLOGY_SNAPSHOT --tenants 80 --profile mix-heavy --duration 1800 --out report.json

- Run a quick CI smoke in Buildkite (example job step):

  - label: "GPU fairness smoke"
    command: |
      bin/infra-benchmark --ci --snapshot ${SNAPSHOT} --tenants 24 --duration 300 --out ci-report.json
    agents:
      queue: ci-gpu-ephemeral

Interpreting results
- Primary signals: per-tenant 95th latency, eviction rate per 1k requests, tokens-per-dollar variance.
- Inequity score > 0.18: investigate allocator packing thresholds and preemption fallback ordering.
- Single-tenant slowdown with low eviction rate: check NVLink adjacency, PCIe contention and device thermal logs.
- Elevated eviction rate with correlated cache_miss: indicates shared KV-cache pressure — consider increasing cache partitioning or pinning hot prefixes.

Fairness metrics computed
- Per-tenant 95p latency normalized by median.
- Tokens-per-dollar coefficient of variation (CV).
- Inequity score (Gini-inspired): composite of latency and cost deviations.
- Tail concentration metric: percentage of total SLO violations attributable to top-3 offenders.

Automated gates and CI integration
- CI will fail if: inequity_score > 0.18 OR mean SLO_violation_fraction across tenants increases by > 15% relative to baseline snapshot.
- Reports are uploaded to the artifacts bucket at gs://redwood-infra-bench/reports/${BUILD_ID}/. A badge and summary are posted to the PR.

Runbook: triage checklist if the benchmark fails
1. Confirm topology snapshot matches the intended test (region, pool type, kernel set).
2. Open the report.json and check: top 5 tenants by SLO violations; eviction map; tokens-per-dollar heatmap.
3. Reproduce a focused run with the offending tenant(s) in isolation (tenants 1..5).
4. If allocator changes were introduced, roll back or disable the allocator feature-flag and re-run.
5. If noise indicates hardware (thermal / pcie): escalate to hw-allocator channel and attach node-level telemetry.
6. File a regression ticket with labels: infra-fairness, blocker, perf-regression.

Ownership and cadence
- Owning team: infra-platform (capacity and allocator engineers).
- Primary owner: Aisha Patel (author).
- CI cadence: nightly full benchmark, PR-level smoke for allocator and packing changes.
- Reviewers: Marcus Nguyen (allocator), Elena García (SRE capacity).

Appendix: example JSON profile (single tenant)
{
  "name": "tenant-sim-A",
  "rps": "1.8",
  "seq_len_p10_p50_p90": "2,32,128",
  "cache_hit": "0.18",
  "burst_factor": "0.5"
}

Appendix: suggested improvements and future work
- Add hardware contention models for shared PCIe/NVLink and pack them into placement simulation.
- Integrate tenant identity aware billing traces to validate tokens-per-dollar calibration.
- Expand to multi-region cross-account bursting scenarios and incorporate egress throttling models.

Related artifacts and links
- Shadow-run telemetry dashboard: infra/fairness/shadow-runs (internal link)
- CI job: pipelines/infra/gpu-fairness-smoke (Buildkite)

If you have questions or want the harness extended to a new tenant type, ping @aisha (Slack) or file an infra-platform improvement ticket and assign to the owner.
